Mesillat Yesharim 4:41: That is, that time is given to the sinner, and he is not cut off from the earth immediately when he sins.
Mesillat Yesharim 4:42: And that the punishment itself is not so severe as to bring destruction.
Mesillat Yesharim 4:43: And that repentance is granted to sinners as an act of pure kindness, such that the uprooting of the will is counted as the uprooting of the deed.
Mesillat Yesharim 4:44: That is, when the penitent recognizes his sin and confesses it, and reflects upon its wickedness, and repents of it and regrets it with a complete regret from the outset — exactly like the regret that annuls a vow — being wholly consoled, wishing and yearning that the thing had never been done at all, and grieving in his heart with intense pain over the fact that the thing was already done, and abandoning it for the future and fleeing from it — then the uprooting of the matter from his will is counted for him as the uprooting of the vow, and he is atoned for. This is what Scripture says (Isaiah 6:7): "and your iniquity shall depart, and your sin shall be atoned for" — meaning that the iniquity truly departs from existence and is uprooted through his present grieving and regretting over what had been done beforehand.
Mesillat Yesharim 4:45: And this is certainly a kindness that goes beyond the strict letter of the law; but in any case it is a kindness that does not entirely deny the law, for there is indeed a basis on which to ground it.
Mesillat Yesharim 4:46: For in place of the will that consented to the sin and the pleasure that he derived from it, there now comes regret and grief.
Mesillat Yesharim 4:47: And likewise, the length of time before punishment is not a waiver of the sin, but merely a measure of patience to open for him an opportunity for rectification.
Mesillat Yesharim 4:48: And so too all the other ways of kindness — such as the matter of "a son confers merit upon a father" (Sanhedrin 104a), or "part of the soul is as the whole soul" (Kohelet Rabbah 7:27), mentioned in the words of the Sages — these are ways of kindness, to accept the small as though it were much; but they do not truly contradict or deny the attribute of justice, for there is already a proper reason to give them weight.
Mesillat Yesharim 4:49: But that transgressions should simply be waived entirely, or that He should pay them no heed at all — this would be entirely against justice, for then there would be no true judgment or law in matters at all; therefore this can never occur. And if the sinner cannot find one of the ways of escape we have mentioned, certainly the attribute of justice will not return empty-handed. And so they said, of blessed memory (Yerushalmi Ta'anit 2): "He is patient, but He collects His due."
Mesillat Yesharim 4:50: It follows that a person who wishes to open his eyes has no enticement by which he could be enticed to refrain from being watchful over his deeds with the utmost watchfulness, and to be exacting with them to the utmost exactness. All these are the reflections that a person should ponder, and through them he will surely acquire the trait of watchfulness — if he is a person of soul.
Mesillat Yesharim 5:1:
An Explanation of the Things That Undermine Watchfulness, and How to Distance Oneself from Them
Now, the things that undermine this trait and distance a person from it are three.
Mesillat Yesharim 5:2: The first is worldly concerns and preoccupation; the second, frivolity and jesting; the third, bad company. Let us speak of them one by one.
Mesillat Yesharim 5:3: As for worldly concerns and preoccupation, we have already spoken of them above; for when a person is preoccupied with the affairs of his world, his thoughts are bound by the chains of the burden that is upon him, and it is impossible for him to give his attention to his conduct.
Mesillat Yesharim 5:4: And the Sages, peace be upon them, seeing this, said (Avot 4:10): "Engage little in business, and occupy yourself with Torah."
Mesillat Yesharim 5:5: For engaging in business is necessary for a person for the sake of his livelihood, but it is not necessary that this engagement be so great that it leaves him no room for his service; therefore we were commanded to set fixed times for Torah study.
Mesillat Yesharim 5:6: And we have already noted that Torah is what a person needs most in order to attain watchfulness, as Rabbi Pinchas said: Torah leads to watchfulness — and without it he will not attain it at all. This is what our Sages, of blessed memory, said (ibid., ch. 2): "nor is an ignorant person pious."
Mesillat Yesharim 5:7: This is because the Creator, blessed be His Name, who created the evil inclination in man, is the One who created the Torah as its seasoning, as our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Kiddushin 30b): "I created the evil inclination, I created for it the Torah as a seasoning."
Mesillat Yesharim 5:8: And it is obvious that if the Creator created no remedy for this affliction other than this one, it is impossible in any way for a person to be healed of this affliction without this remedy; and whoever thinks he can be saved without it is simply mistaken, and he will see his mistake in the end, when he dies in his sin.
Mesillat Yesharim 5:9: For the evil inclination is truly very powerful in man, and without a person's knowledge it keeps growing and gaining strength in him and ruling over him. And if he employs every stratagem in the world but does not take the remedy created for him, which is the Torah, as I have written, he will not know or feel the intensification of his sickness until he dies in his sin and his soul is lost.
Mesillat Yesharim 5:10: To what may this be compared? To a sick man who consulted physicians, who identified his illness and told him to take this medicine; but he, without any prior knowledge of the art of medicine, sets aside that medicine and takes whatever medicines occur to his own mind — will that sick man not certainly die?
Mesillat Yesharim 5:11: So it is with this matter. For no one recognizes the sickness of the evil inclination and the power implanted within it except its own Creator who created it, and He has warned us that its remedy is the Torah. Who, then, would set it aside and take something else instead, and expect to live? Certainly the darkness of materiality will keep gaining strength over him, level after level, and he will not understand, until he finds himself sunk in evil and so very far from the truth that not even a thought of seeking the truth will occur to his heart.
Mesillat Yesharim 5:12: But if he engages in Torah, seeing its ways, its commands, and its warnings, then in the end an awakening will of itself be renewed within him, which will bring him to the good path. This is what our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Petichta of Eichah Rabbati): "Would that they had forsaken Me, and kept My Torah" — for the light within it would bring them back to the good.
Mesillat Yesharim 5:13: And included in this too is setting fixed times for reckoning one's deeds and rectifying them, as I have written above.
Mesillat Yesharim 5:14: And besides all this, whatever leisure remains to him from his labors — if he is wise, he will certainly not waste it, but will seize it at once and not let it go, to occupy himself with the concern of his soul and the rectification of his service.
Mesillat Yesharim 5:15: And this undermining factor, although it is the most general one, is the easiest for one who wishes to escape it to actually escape from.
Mesillat Yesharim 5:16: But the second is very difficult, and it is frivolity and jesting. For whoever is drowning in these is like one drowning in the great sea, from which it is very hard to be rescued. For frivolity destroys a person's heart, so that reason and understanding no longer rule over him, and he is like a drunkard or a madman, whom it is impossible to advise or to guide, for they do not accept guidance.
Mesillat Yesharim 5:17: This is what King Solomon, peace be upon him, said (Ecclesiastes 2:2): "Of laughter I said, it is mad; and of mirth, what does it accomplish?" And the Sages, of blessed memory, said (Avot 3:13): "Frivolity and levity accustom a person to sexual immorality." For even though sexual immorality is a grave matter to every person of understanding, whose heart fears to come near it because of the impression already formed in his mind of the true gravity of its transgression and the severity of its punishment — nevertheless, frivolity and levity draw him little by little and bring him ever closer, so that the fear gradually departs from him, level after level, until he reaches the sin itself and commits it.
Mesillat Yesharim 5:18: And why is this so? Because just as the entire existence of watchfulness depends on paying attention to the matter, so too the whole essence of frivolity is nothing but the removal of attention from straight, reflective thoughts, so that thoughts of fear do not enter his heart at all.
Mesillat Yesharim 5:19: And you will see how severe jesting is and how greatly destructive, for just like a shield coated with oil, which causes arrows to slip off and fall to the ground and not reach the person's body, so too jesting deflects rebuke and reproof; for with a single jest and a small laugh, a person can cast off from himself a great deal of the arousal and stirring that his heart would otherwise experience of itself upon seeing or hearing matters that would arouse him to reckoning and self-examination of his deeds.
Mesillat Yesharim 5:20: And by the power of jesting he casts it all to the ground and it makes no impression on him at all — not because of any weakness in the matters themselves, nor because of any lack of understanding in his heart, but because of the power of jesting, which demolishes all matters of ethical instruction and fear.
Mesillat Yesharim 5:21: And indeed, the prophet Isaiah cried out against this like a crane, for he saw that this was what left no room for his rebukes to make any impression, and destroyed the hope of sinners; this is what he said (Isaiah 28:22): "Now therefore be not jesters, lest your bonds be made strong."
Mesillat Yesharim 5:22: And the Sages, of blessed memory, have already decreed (Avodah Zarah 18b) that the jester brings suffering upon himself, and this is what Scripture itself states explicitly (Proverbs 19:29): "Judgments are prepared for jesters" — for this is a matter that justice itself dictates: whoever is moved by reflection and by study need not be chastised in his body, for he will already turn back from his sins without this, through the stirrings of repentance that are born in his heart from what he reads or hears of ethical teachings and rebukes.
Mesillat Yesharim 5:23: But jesters, who are not moved by rebukes because of the power of their jesting, have no remedy except judgments — for their jesting will have no power to deflect these from them as it deflects ethical teachings.
Mesillat Yesharim 5:24: And according to the gravity of the sin and its consequences, the true Judge deals more severely in His punishment; and this is what our Sages, of blessed memory, taught us (Avodah Zarah 18b): "Jesting is severe, for it begins in suffering and ends in destruction, as it is said: lest your bonds be made strong, for I have heard a decree of destruction, etc."
Mesillat Yesharim 5:25: And the third undermining factor is company — that is, the company of fools and sinners; and this is what Scripture says (Proverbs 13:20): "and a companion of fools shall be broken." For we see, many times, that even after a person has become convinced of the obligation of the service and of the watchfulness it requires, he grows lax in it, or transgresses some of it, so that his companions will not mock him, or in order to fit in with them.
Mesillat Yesharim 5:26: This is what Solomon warns and says (ibid. 24:21): "and do not associate with dissenters." For if a person tells you (Ketubot 17a), "A person's mind should always be sociable with others," you should answer him: this applies only to people who act as human beings should act, but not to people who act like beasts. And Solomon further warns (ibid. 14:7): "Go from the presence of a foolish man." And King David said (Psalms 1:1): "Happy is the man who has not walked, etc." — and our Sages, of blessed memory, already explained (Avodah Zarah 18b): if he walked, he will end up standing; and if he stood, he will end up sitting. And it says (Psalms 26:4-5): "I have not sat with men of falsehood... I have hated the assembly of evildoers, etc."
Mesillat Yesharim 5:27: A person has no choice but to purify and cleanse himself, and to keep his feet from the ways of the masses who are sunk in the vanities of the age, and to turn his feet back toward the courts of the Lord and His dwelling places. This is what David himself concludes, saying (ibid. 26:6): "I will wash my hands in innocence, and I will go about Your altar, O Lord."
Mesillat Yesharim 5:28: And should it happen that he finds himself in the company of one who mocks him, he should not pay any heed to that mockery; on the contrary, he should mock his mockers and hold them in contempt, and consider in his own mind: if he stood to gain a great deal of money, would he give up what was needed for that on account of his companions, so that they would not mock him?! All the more so, then, should he not be willing to lose his soul on account of mockery.
Mesillat Yesharim 5:29: And in this vein our Sages, of blessed memory, warned (Avot 5:20): "Be bold as a leopard... to do the will of your Father in Heaven." And David said (Psalms 119:46): "And I will speak of Your testimonies before kings, and will not be ashamed."
Mesillat Yesharim 5:30: For even though most kings occupy themselves and speak of matters of grandeur and pleasure, and David, who was also a king, would seemingly be shamed if, while in their company, he were to speak words of ethical teaching and Torah, instead of telling of great things and human pleasures as they did — nevertheless he did not concern himself with this at all, and his heart was not enticed by these vanities, since he had already attained the truth; rather he explains and says: "And I will speak of Your testimonies before kings, and will not be ashamed." And Isaiah likewise said (Isaiah 50:7): "Therefore I have set my face like flint, and I know that I shall not be ashamed."
